caseStudy.title: Ethio School Platform
caseStudy.cardDesc: One platform for a whole school: attendance, homework, grades and parent communication, designed phone-first for Ethiopian schools.
caseStudy.subtitle: A school management and learning platform where leaders, teachers, students and parents work from the same up-to-date picture.

caseStudy.overview:
Ethio School Platform brings a school's daily work into one place: attendance, homework and submissions, weighted grading, a digital library, announcements and messages.

Each of the four roles (administrator, teacher, student and parent) gets its own dashboard and menu, in English or Amharic, designed first for affordable phones.

process.intro: I treated privacy as the foundation, not a feature: the rules for who can see what were written and tested in the database before any screen was built.
steps: Brief and scope: the four roles, the daily jobs of each, and a 10-step demo story from 'admin creates Grade 8A' to 'parent sees the grade'.
Data model and security: tables for the school year, classes, work and communication, with Row Level Security on every table and tests that try to break it.
A demo school (fictional) that works in any browser, applying the same rules as the database.
Role experiences one milestone at a time: shell and dashboards, then teaching, administration and communication.
Testing on five screen widths (375 to 1280 px) and walking the whole homework story in automated browser tests.

caseStudy.problem:
Many schools still run on attendance books, paper mark sheets and files in different places, so it is slow to know how a class is really doing.

Parents often learn about missed homework or falling grades at the end of a term, and school communication is spread across personal phones and group chats the school doesn't control.

caseStudy.insight: If parents see the same information as teachers while the term is still going, a small problem can be solved before it becomes a failed term.

caseStudy.solution:
One platform with a role-based experience: leaders get school-wide analytics and a list of students requiring academic attention; teachers take attendance, post work and grade from a phone; students see what's due and their feedback; parents follow each child in real time.

Grades are weighted the way each school decides (for example homework 10%, final exam 30%), and class averages are shown without ever revealing another student's grade.

Messaging follows rules the school sets, so families reach the right teacher without sharing personal numbers.

caseStudy.outcome:
A working MVP with four complete role experiences, built in four milestones: sign-in and dashboards, teaching, administration, and communication.

Privacy is enforced in the database itself: a student sees only their own records, a parent only their children, a teacher only their classes. Database tests try to break every rule.

Automated browser tests walk the full homework story and every role at five screen widths, from 375 px phones to 1280 px desktops.

Next: a guided demo tour, the remaining Amharic translations, deployment with real sign-in, and a pilot with a school.
